# Words and phrases

Lexical tells and wordy phrasing. Word lists are triggers to inspect, not automatic deletions: a listed word used in its plain sense stays.

Tags: strength (`hard` always · `default` unless an exception or the sensitivity says otherwise · `soft` preference) · kind (`ai-tell`, `clarity`, `both`, `procedure`).

### LEX-001 · core AI vocabulary (tier 1)
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Do not reach for the core AI-favoured vocabulary when writing; use it only when it is the plainest accurate word, and when reviewing text treat several of these words together as the signal.

- Threshold: **standard:** writing: avoid each word unless it is the plainest accurate term; reviewing: flag a paragraph with 2+ distinct list words, or one word repeated across the piece · **strict:** writing or reviewing: replace any single occurrence that is not the plainest accurate word · **relaxed:** flag only a paragraph with 3+ distinct list words
- Triggers: `delve`, `delving`, `tapestry`, `rich tapestry`, `realm`, `testament`, `a testament to`, `pivotal`, `intricate`, `intricacies`, `meticulous`, `meticulously`, `underscore (verb)`, `underscores`, `showcase`, `showcasing`, `garner`, `garnered`, `interplay`, `vibrant`, `multifaceted`, `foster`, `fostering`, `bolster`, `bolstered`, `landscape (abstract)`, `paradigm (figurative)`, `synergy`, `embark`, `beacon`, `symphony`, `kaleidoscope`, `ever-evolving`, `holistic`, `deep dive`, `unpack (figurative)`, `crucial`, `leverage (verb)`, `streamline`, `robust (figurative)`, `revolutionize`, `unleash`, `unlock (hype)`, `supercharge`, `elevate your`, `embrace (figurative)`, `hit differently`, `watershed moment`, `nexus`, `liminal`, `additionally`, `align with`, `landscape`, `robust`, `seamless`, `underscore`, `comprehensive`, `empower`, `harness`, `game-changer`, `unlock`, `notably`, `furthermore`, `groundbreaking`, `shed light on`, `pave the way`
- Exceptions: literal or technical senses: robust statistics/estimator, leverage in finance, landscape orientation or terrain, streamline in fluid dynamics, unlock a mutex/account; quoted speech, titles, names and text being analysed; a single hit is a hypothesis, not proof of machine authorship; never accuse on one word; the replacement must change the thought, not just swap a synonym (see LEX-040)
- Example: ✗ The report delves into the intricate landscape of cache invalidation, underscoring its pivotal role. → ✓ The report covers when the cache goes stale and what that costs.

### LEX-002 · cluster-only inflated vocabulary (tier 2)
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Treat individually normal but AI-inflated words as a signal only when they stack; rewrite the passage when two or more appear together.

- Threshold: **standard:** flag a paragraph with 2+ distinct list words, or 3+ in a short piece · **strict:** flag any paragraph with 2+ distinct list words · **relaxed:** flag a paragraph with 3+ distinct list words
- Triggers: `harness (figurative)`, `navigate (figurative)`, `elevate`, `empower`, `spearhead`, `resonate`, `underpin`, `underpinning`, `underpinnings`, `nuanced`, `encompass`, `ecosystem (figurative)`, `framework (figurative)`, `myriad`, `plethora`, `catalyze`, `reimagine`, `galvanize`, `augment`, `cultivate`, `illuminate`, `elucidate`, `juxtapose`, `paradigm-shifting`, `transformation`, `transformative`, `cornerstone`, `paramount`, `poised`, `burgeoning`, `nascent`, `quintessential`, `overarching`, `comprehensive`, `enhance`, `highlight (verb)`, `key (adjective)`, `valuable`, `align with`, `daunting`, `impactful`, `actionable`, `learnings`, `best practices`, `thought leader`, `thought leadership`, `keen`, `intertwine`, `entwine`, `weave`, `grapple`, `unravel`, `unveil`, `transcend`, `reverberate`, `exemplify`, `amplify`, `glean`, `strive`, `thrive`, `flourishing`, `indelible`, `poignant`, `profound`, `captivating`, `unparalleled`, `unwavering`, `relentless`, `tireless`, `invaluable`, `noteworthy`, `commendable`, `exemplary`, `versatile`, `pervasive`, `whimsical`, `thought-provoking`, `crucible`, `enigma`, `epicenter`, `linchpin`, `pinnacle`, `bedrock`, `hallmark`, `foray`, `quest`, `journey (figurative)`, `lens (figurative)`, `facet`, `trajectory`, `treasure trove`, `paradigm shift`, `enduring`
- Exceptions: one occurrence is not a finding; technical terms of art: test harness, software framework, package ecosystem, key (cryptographic, lookup), navigate (UI); words excluded from all lists as normal domain vocabulary: optimize, maximize, promote, hinder, tailor, craft, uncover, scalable (as metric), sustainable, granular, systemic, mission-critical, milestone, roadmap, toolkit, stakeholders, deliverables, bandwidth (network), touchpoint, catalyst (chemistry); quoted speech and analysed text
- Example: ✗ This comprehensive framework empowers teams to navigate a burgeoning ecosystem. → ✓ The guide lists which three services each team owns.

### LEX-003 · vague-praise word density (tier 3)
`soft · both · scope: prose · voice can override`

When one vague-praise word recurs often in a piece, replace most uses with a number, comparison or example.

- Threshold: **standard:** same form used max(3, 3% of words) times or more · **strict:** same form used 2+ times per 500 words · **relaxed:** same form used 5+ times per 500 words
- Triggers: `significant`, `significantly`, `innovative`, `innovation`, `effective`, `effectively`, `dynamic`, `dynamics`, `scalable`, `scalability`, `compelling`, `unprecedented`, `exceptional`, `exceptionally`, `remarkable`, `remarkably`, `sophisticated`, `instrumental`, `world-class`, `state-of-the-art`, `best-in-class`, `verbatim`
- Exceptions: statistical 'significant' with a test behind it; 'state-of-the-art' when citing a benchmark result; quoted text
- Example: ✗ A significant, innovative change that significantly improves an effective pipeline. → ✓ The change cuts build time from 9 to 4 minutes.

### LEX-004 · era / model-specific vocabulary watch-list
`soft · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Keep a dated watch-list of words favoured by recent or specific models and apply the same cluster test; refresh it rather than trusting an old list.

- Threshold: **standard:** flag 3+ distinct watch-list words in a paragraph · **strict:** flag 2+ distinct watch-list words in a paragraph · **relaxed:** report only, never rewrite on this alone
- Triggers: `challenge`, `clearer`, `dependable`, `echoed`, `foster`, `leverage`, `matters`, `multifaceted`, `practical`, `prioritize`, `quietly`, `steady`, `universally`, `causal`, `empirical`, `correlate`
- Exceptions: these are ordinary words; only density counts; empirical/causal/correlate in actual statistics or science writing; the list ages: tag entries with the model era and retire stale ones
- Example: ✗ A practical, dependable and steady approach that quietly matters. → ✓ The approach has run for a year without a failed deploy.

### LEX-005 · copula avoidance
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Say 'is', 'are' or 'has' when a sentence only states what something is or has, instead of serves as, stands as, boasts, features, marks or represents; define a thing directly rather than saying its name refers to something.

- Threshold: **standard:** replace when the verb adds nothing; flag 2+ in a paragraph · **strict:** replace any single copula substitute that does not add meaning · **relaxed:** flag only 3+ in a paragraph
- Triggers: `serves as`, `stands as`, `features`, `marks`, `represents`, `functions as`, `operates as`, `boasts`, `offers`, `maintains`, `refers to`, `represents a`, `offers a`, `ventured into`, `began his career as`
- Exceptions: the verb enumerates, defines, locates or names a real role ('serves three failure modes', 'represents the user in the token', 'the server offers TLS 1.3'); 'refers to' in glossary entries about words themselves, or for pointers between documents; do not hold copula verbs in a flat ban list
- Example: ✗ The module serves as the entry point and boasts a retry queue. → ✓ The module is the entry point and has a retry queue.

### LEX-006 · significance / legacy puffery
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Do not inflate importance with stock significance words; state the concrete effect instead.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `a pivotal moment`, `contributing to`, `crucial`, `crucial role`, `deeply rooted`, `define the next era`, `enduring legacy`, `evolution of`, `evolving landscape`, `exciting times ahead`, `focal point`, `fundamentally reshape`, `highlighting`, `indelible mark`, `is a testament`, `key turning point`, `lasting impact`, `lasting legacy`, `marking the`, `pivotal`, `pivotal moment`, `plays a key role`, `plays a vital role`, `reflecting broader trends`, `reflects a broader`, `reflects broader`, `setting the stage for`, `shaping the`, `something entirely new`, `stands as`, `stands as a testament`, `testament`, `testament to`, `the future looks bright`, `underscores its importance`, `underscoring`, `vital`, `watershed`
- Exceptions: a sourced historical claim that something was a turning point; quoted text; 'vital' and 'key' in medical or cryptographic senses; the source documents the significance (a cited historian, measured impact); the same or next sentence supplies the mechanism, measurement or evidence that earns the claim (PRC-019); literal uses ('serves as the entry point', 'contributing to the repo')
- Example: ✗ The migration is a pivotal step that leaves an indelible mark on the platform. → ✓ The migration moved login to the new service.

### LEX-007 · promotional adjectives
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Replace promotional and brochure adjectives, and stacks of hyphenated modifiers, with a statement of what the thing does.

- Threshold: **standard:** any single occurrence in neutral text (docs, comments, commits, reports); 2+ in marketing copy · **strict:** any single occurrence · **relaxed:** 2+ in a paragraph
- Triggers: `groundbreaking`, `seamless`, `seamlessly`, `robust`, `cutting-edge`, `breathtaking`, `stunning`, `nestled`, `boasts`, `in the heart of`, `vibrant`, `rich tapestry`, `game-changing`, `world-class`, `best-in-class`, `bustling`, `future-proof`, `nestled in the heart of`, `renowned`, `must-try`, `diverse array`, `profound`, `exemplifies`, `commitment to`
- Exceptions: the user's own marketing copy in a voice profile that wants it (style only); quoted reviews or product names
- Example: ✗ A cutting-edge, seamless, best-in-class sync engine. → ✓ The sync engine pushes changes to open tabs within a second.

### LEX-008 · hype and launch copy
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Cut hype phrases, launch-copy introductions, slogans and slot-fill templates; say what the product is and what it does.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `a [adj] step towards`, `a game-changer`, `a major step forward for`, `batteries included`, `boasts a`, `breathtaking`, `commitment to`, `diverse array`, `dynamic blend`, `enhancing`, `enter [product].`, `exciting possibilities lie ahead`, `exemplifies`, `featuring`, `groundbreaking`, `groundbreaking advancement`, `in the heart of`, `it just works`, `meet [product], your new favorite`, `mind-blowing`, `must-visit`, `natural beauty`, `nestled`, `paving the way for`, `profound`, `pushing the boundaries`, `redefine the future`, `renowned`, `represents a significant milestone`, `revolutionizing the way`, `rich (figurative)`, `rich cultural heritage`, `sane defaults`, `say hello to [product]`, `showcasing`, `small enough to fit in your head`, `stunning`, `think x meets y`, `this changes everything`, `unlocking the power of`, `vibrant`, `zero config`
- Exceptions: names or slogans quoted from a real source; a concrete behaviour the source supplies may replace the slogan; marketing copy the user explicitly requested; quoted reviews; literal senses (rich soil, profound hearing loss)
- Example: ✗ Meet Ledgerly, your new favorite way to reconcile; it just works. → ✓ Ledgerly matches bank lines to invoices by amount and date.

### LEX-009 · corporate jargon and boilerplate
`default · both · scope: all · voice can override`

Replace corporate jargon and press-release boilerplate with the plain action or fact.

- Threshold: **standard:** any single occurrence of an idiom (circle back, double down, lean into, touch base); 2+ distinct boilerplate phrases per piece · **strict:** any single occurrence · **relaxed:** 2+ in a paragraph
- Triggers: `active social media presence`, `align with`, `aligns with`, `amplify`, `as per`, `at your earliest convenience`, `bandwidth`, `circle back`, `commitment to`, `community-driven`, `dedicated to excellence`, `dedication to`, `double down`, `emerging sector`, `kindly`, `lean into`, `long-term sustainability`, `maintains a strong digital presence`, `moving forward`, `on the same page`, `pain point`, `per my last`, `please find attached`, `take a step back`, `the integration of`, `the intersection of`, `touch base`, `user engagement`, `value proposition`, `wanted to reach out`
- Exceptions: literal senses (network bandwidth, a value proposition section in a business plan template); local email convention the user's voice profile keeps (style only); established technical terms of the field are not jargon: keep the one that is most precise and define it on first use (LEX-047); quoting an organisation's own statement with attribution
- Example: ✗ Let's circle back and double down on user engagement moving forward. → ✓ Next week we will retest the sign-up flow.

### LEX-010 · dead metaphors and invented labels
`default · both · scope: all · voice can override`

Replace abstract metaphor nouns, coined jargon and invented concept labels with the concrete word or a plain description; define any genuine named pattern at first use.

- Threshold: **standard:** any single metaphor noun used figuratively; invented labels at 2+ per piece · **strict:** any single occurrence · **relaxed:** invented labels at 3+ per piece
- Triggers: `bedrock`, `creep`, `divide`, `endgame`, `evacuate (move code)`, `flywheel`, `gold-plating`, `harness (metaphor)`, `inversion`, `load-bearing`, `locus`, `modality`, `nexus`, `north star`, `paradigm`, `paradox`, `primitive (noun)`, `ratchet (metaphor)`, `scaffolding (metaphor)`, `substrate`, `surface (api surface)`, `swiss army knife`, `trap`, `vacuum`, `vantage`, `vector`, `wedge`
- Exceptions: established terms of art: attack vector, primitive types, API surface where the codebase uses it, scaffolding tools, physical load-bearing walls; 'load-bearing' only flags when it modifies an abstract noun (assumption, claim, invariant) on the same line; a label the text defines and then uses consistently; live figurative language is not a dead metaphor: keep metaphors and one-sentence metaphor paragraphs that carry meaning, especially ones built on a specific ordinary person, and any metaphor whose removal would lose something the reader needs; an analogy the reader needs to grasp an unfamiliar idea, and that is shorter than the literal description, may stay once; flag stacked, decorative or unexplained imagery, not every figure; quoted speech; technical terms that happen to be metaphors (thread, pipe, tree)
- Example: ✗ This is the north star of our flywheel, a wedge against the supervision paradox. → ✓ Our goal is fewer manual reviews; each review costs about an hour.

### LEX-011 · wordy stock phrases
`soft · clarity · scope: all · voice can override`

Shorten wordy stock phrases to their plain form (in order to -> to, due to the fact that -> because, the question as to whether -> whether).

- Threshold: **standard:** 2+ in a paragraph, or the same phrase repeated in a piece · **strict:** any single occurrence · **relaxed:** report only
- Triggers: `in order to`, `due to the fact that`, `the question as to whether`, `there is no doubt but that`, `used for ... purposes`, `in a ... manner`, `he is a man who`, `this is a subject which`, `as to whether`, `the fact that`, `owing to the fact that`, `in spite of the fact that`, `along these lines`, `one of the most`, `in terms of`, `in the event that`, `we perform a regression`, `we conduct a regression`, `we carry out a regression`
- Exceptions: this is a clarity edit, not evidence of AI authorship; an occasional wordy phrase is human and fine; stripping every one creates its own flat pattern; legal or quoted text; keep a fronted topic phrase (for X, regarding X, in terms of X) when it limits the scope of the claim; keep the shell list narrow: only noun-heavy action shells (carried out an optimisation of, achieved an improvement in) restore to the plain verb; ordinary nominalisation is not a target (STR-028)
- Example: ✗ Due to the fact that the job failed, in order to recover we reran it. → ✓ Because the job failed, we reran it.

### LEX-012 · plain word over fancy synonym
`soft · clarity · scope: all · voice can override`

Prefer the short everyday word to a stiff or euphemistic synonym unless the longer word is more precise.

- Threshold: **standard:** replace when the plain word means the same · **strict:** replace any stiff synonym · **relaxed:** report only
- Triggers: `utilize`, `facilitate`, `commence`, `ascertain`, `endeavor`, `numerous`, `possess`, `authored`, `relocated`, `attempted`, `passed away`, `perform (as do)`
- Exceptions: formal register is not an AI sign by itself; precise technical senses ('perform' a test, 'state' in a state machine); 'passed away' in condolence messages
- Example: ✗ We utilized the script to facilitate the migration. → ✓ We used the script to run the migration.

### LEX-013 · omit needless words
`default · clarity · scope: all · voice can override`

Omit needless words, padding nouns and redundant relative clauses, without stripping detail or making the text terse.

- Threshold: **standard:** cut padding that adds no meaning; keep rhythm and detail · **strict:** cut every padding noun and redundant clause · **relaxed:** report only
- Triggers: `case`, `character`, `each and every`, `factor`, `feature`, `first and foremost`, `nature`, `plays a key role in`, `respectively`, `serves to highlight`, `system`, `various different`, `viewpoint`
- Exceptions: the noun names a real thing (a test case, a system under test); do not compress to telegraphic fragments; never remove facts, qualifiers needed for accuracy, or steps; context a new reader needs even if earlier readers know it; required legal or template boilerplate; a trimmed answer that drops a required caveat, condition or next step fails: length stays proportional to stakes in both directions; hedges, qualifiers and connectives that carry meaning (INT-003); rhythm in voice-licensed text
- Example: ✗ Trafalgar, which was a battle of a decisive character, ended the threat. → ✓ Trafalgar, a decisive battle, ended the threat.

### LEX-014 · concrete over abstract
`default · clarity · scope: all · voice cannot override`

Use the specific, concrete term instead of a general abstraction or a pile of nominalizations.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `we examine the relationship between`, `we explore the relationship between`, `we investigate the relationship between`
- Exceptions: deliberate abstraction in a summary that is followed by specifics; when a figure, time or object is already given in the same or an adjacent paragraph, move it into the place of the vague summary phrase instead of leaving both; when the source gives no specifics, leave the abstract sentence abstract or simplify it; never invent the specifics (INT-001, INT-002); never manufacture the specific (INT-001); earned compression stays compressed (PRC-019)
- Example: ✗ An issue occurred regarding the facilitation of data synchronization. → ✓ The sync job crashed.

### LEX-015 · one name per thing (no elegant variation)
`default · both · scope: all · voice cannot override`

Call each thing by one name and each action by one verb throughout; repeat the term rather than cycling synonyms.

- Threshold: **standard:** a referent named 2+ different ways · **strict:** any renamed referent · **relaxed:** 3+ different names
- Exceptions: when reviewing others' text, synonym variety is weak evidence: many writers were taught to avoid repetition; a pronoun is fine where the referent is clear; writers taught to avoid repetition (common in non-native English) show this too; treat as clarity, weak as an AI sign
- Example: ✗ The worker starts the job; the daemon then initiates the task. → ✓ The worker starts the job, then starts the next job.

### LEX-016 · literal-reader wording
`soft · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

Avoid idioms, Latin abbreviations and words that collide with a term of art when the audience may read literally, translate, or know that term.

- Threshold: **standard:** flag idioms in procedures and reference docs; flag term-of-art collisions · **strict:** flag every idiom and Latin abbreviation · **relaxed:** report only
- Triggers: `e.g.`, `i.e.`, `etc.`, `proof (outside a formal proof)`, `proof point`
- Exceptions: e.g./i.e. are acceptable in most English prose and in code comments where local convention uses them; casual voice profiles
- Example: ✗ This proof point shows the scheme is secure, i.e. ballpark safe. → ✓ This benchmark shows the scheme resists the known attacks.

### LEX-017 · precise usage: fact, while
`soft · clarity · scope: all · voice can override`

Use 'fact' only for verifiable matters, and do not use 'while' loosely where 'and', 'but' or 'although' is meant.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `fact`, `while`, `models where`
- Exceptions: temporal 'while'; factual tradeoffs joined by 'while' where the sense is clear
- Example: ✗ While the API is fast, the docs are thin; the fact is it is the best option. → ✓ The API is fast, but the docs are thin. We think it is the best option.

### LEX-018 · unnecessary hyphenation
`soft · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not add hyphens to open or closed compounds that do not take them; keep hyphens in compound modifiers before a noun.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `code-base`, `data-set`, `time-frame`, `road-map`, `in real-time`, `out-of-the-box`
- Exceptions: attributive use before a noun ('real-time updates'); house style that hyphenates; common established compounds (long-term, well-known) are fine
- Example: ✗ The code-base updates in real-time. → ✓ The codebase updates in real time.

### LEX-019 · signposting and emphasis crutches
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Cut signposting and emphasis phrases that tell the reader something matters, including attitude adverbs; let the content show it.

- Threshold: **standard:** any single 'it's worth noting / it's important to note' frame or crutch line (Full stop. Let that sink in.); attitude adverbs at 2+ per piece · **strict:** any single occurrence · **relaxed:** 2+ frames per piece
- Triggers: `a comment is in order`, `always check before`, `an important question in the literature is`, `and here's the part most people miss`, `at its core`, `at the end of the day`, `at the heart of`, `cannot be overstated`, `certainly`, `full stop.`, `genuinely`, `here's the interesting part`, `here's what's interesting`, `here's why that matters`, `history is clear`, `importantly`, `in terms of`, `interestingly`, `it bears mentioning`, `it is crucial to differentiate`, `it is easy to show that`, `it is essential to`, `it is important to note that`, `it is worth noting that`, `it should be noted that`, `it's crucial to understand`, `it's important to note`, `it's important to note that`, `it's important to remember`, `it's worth noting`, `it's worth noting that`, `let that sink in.`, `make no mistake`, `notably`, `period.`, `significantly`, `surprisingly`, `the reality is`, `the reality is simpler`, `the reality is that`, `the truth is simple`, `this matters because`, `this paper contributes to the literature by`, `this serves as a reminder`, `this underscores the importance of`, `to prevent confusion`, `undoubtedly`, `when it comes to`, `without a doubt`, `worth mentioning`
- Exceptions: a warning that carries a concrete instruction ('Back up the DB first; the migration drops table X'); 'importantly' or 'notably' once, when it marks the one item among several that changes the decision; when a comment phrase opens a later paragraph and the claim it introduces is real, the fix may name the thing commented on instead of cutting it; never fix it with a bare 'this' that points at a whole clause (STR-047)
- Example: ✗ It's worth noting that the cache is cold. Let that sink in. → ✓ The cache is cold, so the first request takes 3 s.

### LEX-020 · hollow intensifiers and magic adverbs
`default · both · scope: all · voice can override`

Cut hollow intensifiers and emphasis adverbs, or replace the adverb with a stronger verb or a measured number; keep adverbs that carry meaning.

- Threshold: **standard:** a listed intensifier that adds nothing; 'quietly/deeply/fundamentally' as significance props at any count; others at 2+ per paragraph · **strict:** any listed intensifier that can be deleted without changing meaning · **relaxed:** 3+ per paragraph
- Triggers: `genuine`, `genuinely`, `truly`, `quite frankly`, `to be honest`, `let's be clear`, `actually`, `really`, `just`, `literally`, `honestly`, `simply`, `deeply`, `fundamentally`, `inherently`, `inevitably`, `interestingly`, `importantly`, `crucially`, `very`, `so (intensifier)`, `certainly`, `interesting`, `quietly`, `remarkably`, `arguably`, `quickly`, `significantly`, `real (empty intensifier)`, `true (empty intensifier)`, `striking`, `very novel`, `very significant`
- Exceptions: adverbs that change truth value or scope: only, just (= only/recently), probably, usually, often, rarely; 'actually' marking a correction of a named expectation; 'real/actual' when the fake or nominal contrast is named; technical adverbs (lazily evaluated, atomically, asynchronously); 'honestly'/'look' inside an ordinary casual sentence; natural, occasional 'very' in conversational text
- Example: ✗ This genuinely, deeply simplifies the truly real problem. → ✓ This removes two of the five setup steps.

### LEX-021 · stock transitions
`soft · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not use stock connectors (moreover, furthermore, additionally, notably) as glue in place of a real logical link; when a connector is needed, use the one that states the actual relation, and do not make any single connector your default.

- Threshold: **standard:** 3+ stock connectors per 500 words, or the same connector twice in a paragraph · **strict:** any stock connector opening a sentence · **relaxed:** report only
- Triggers: `moreover`, `furthermore`, `additionally`, `in addition`, `notably`, `that said`, `that being said`, `consequently`, `conversely`, `subsequently`, `accordingly`, `thus`, `hence`, `thereby`, `therein`, `thereof`, `herein`, `heretofore`, `whilst`, `amidst`, `notwithstanding`, `nonetheless`, `nevertheless`, `namely`, `akin`, `advent`, `arduous`, `broadly speaking`, `generally speaking`
- Exceptions: transition words alone are weak evidence of AI text; humans and style guides use them; a connector that states a real causal or contrastive relation (however, so, because, therefore) is fine at normal frequency; formal registers (legal, academic) where 'thus', 'hence', 'namely' are conventional; keep an explicit turn marker where the argument actually turns; the target is the connector used as paragraph glue, especially when consecutive paragraphs open with one
- Example: ✗ Moreover, the build is faster. Furthermore, it is smaller. → ✓ The build is also faster and smaller.

### LEX-022 · hedge stacking
`default · both · scope: all · voice cannot override`

Do not stack hedges; keep the one qualifier the evidence needs and drop the rest.

- Threshold: **standard:** 2+ hedges on one claim · **strict:** 2+ hedges on one claim · **relaxed:** 3+ hedges on one claim
- Triggers: `could possibly`, `could potentially`, `could potentially possibly`, `depending on the context`, `in some cases it may`, `it's also possible`, `may eventually`, `might arguably`, `might ultimately`, `one could argue that`, `this is an inference`, `this may potentially indicate`, `to be fair`
- Exceptions: integrity: never delete the qualifier that keeps a claim true (probably, in most cases, usually); natural single qualifiers (perhaps, tends to) are human and fine; necessary qualifiers (usually, probably, most) that keep the claim true (integrity overrides); scope statements, legal and safety notices, corrections; ordinary single hedges (perhaps, usually, tends to); real uncertainty, which must stay (criterion 1); a hedge that reflects real uncertainty stays, and may be restored when the source's stance warrants it; cut only stacked or empty hedges
- Example: ✗ This could potentially perhaps reduce latency. → ✓ This could reduce latency.

### LEX-023 · lazy extremes
`default · both · scope: prose · voice cannot override`

Replace sweeping universals (every, always, never, everyone, nobody) with the true scope when they overstate; keep them when they are literally true.

- Threshold: **standard:** flag universals not backed by the text · **strict:** check every universal · **relaxed:** report only
- Triggers: `every`, `always`, `never`, `everyone`, `everybody`, `nobody`
- Exceptions: integrity: a universal that is true ('always returns null on timeout') must stay; do not weaken definite supported claims into vagueness; do not replace with 'most' or 'some' unless that is what the evidence says
- Example: ✗ Everyone hates config files and nobody reads the docs. → ✓ Three of the five users we interviewed skipped the docs.

### LEX-024 · moral-adjective category error
`soft · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not attach moral words (honest, faithful, truthful) to non-agentic technical things or passives, and do not add gratuitous 'every' quantifiers.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `honest`, `honestly`, `faithful`, `faithfully`, `truthful`
- Exceptions: established terms (faithful functor, honest broker, faithful reproduction); people and agents can be honest
- Example: ✗ The schema has an honest shape and every field is flagged honestly. → ✓ The schema matches the data; missing fields are marked null.

### LEX-025 · throat-clearing openers and staged run-ups
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Delete throat-clearing openers, scene-setters, 'let's' invitations and here's-what announcements; start with the content.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `as technology continues to evolve`, `can we talk about`, `heads up`, `here's that [x]`, `here's the problem though`, `here's the thing`, `here's this [x]`, `here's what [x]`, `here's what i find interesting`, `here's what i mean:`, `here's what you need to know`, `here's why [x]`, `honestly?`, `i recently had the pleasure of`, `i'll say it again:`, `i'm going to be honest`, `imagine a world where`, `in a world where`, `in the dynamic world of`, `in the rapidly evolving world of`, `in the realm of`, `in today's`, `in today's digital age`, `in today's ever-evolving world`, `in today's fast-paced world`, `in today's rapidly evolving landscape`, `it turns out`, `let me be clear`, `let's be honest`, `let's break this down`, `let's dive in`, `let's dive into`, `let's examine`, `let's explore`, `let's take a look`, `look,`, `now let's look at`, `now more than ever`, `one of the most important aspects`, `one thing that bit me, so pay attention`, `quick note`, `real talk`, `since the dawn of time`, `the thing is`, `when it comes to`, `whether you're a beginner or an expert`, `whether you're x or y`, `without further ado`
- Exceptions: a heading-like lead that orients a reply to a specific earlier question; fiction and teaching examples that use 'imagine' deliberately; a here's-X line that introduces a code block or list the reader needs
- Example: ✗ In today's fast-paced world, caching matters. Let's dive in. Here's what you need to know: → ✓ Next.js caches data at four layers.

### LEX-026 · fake suspense and teaser hooks
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not tease a reveal or stage candor before an ordinary point (the catch?, here's the kicker, honestly?); state the point.

- Threshold: **standard:** any single standalone teaser fragment; 2+ softer lead-ins (turns out, the truth is) per piece · **strict:** any single occurrence · **relaxed:** 2+ teasers per piece
- Triggers: `the catch?`, `the kicker?`, `here's the thing.`, `but here's the kicker`, `the best part?`, `plot twist:`, `the result?`, `honestly?`, `real talk:`, `here's the thing`, `here's the kicker`, `here's where it gets interesting`, `here's what most people miss`, `but here's the truth`, `but here's what nobody's saying`, `the truth is`, `let's face it`, `you're not imagining it`, `the uncomfortable truth is`, `it turns out`, `spoiler:`, `hint:`
- Exceptions: 'honestly' or 'look' inside an ordinary casual sentence (not a standalone opener); a genuine surprise backed by data, said plainly
- Example: ✗ The kicker? It only runs on Linux. → ✓ It only runs on Linux.

### LEX-027 · canned closers and recap formulas
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Do not end with a canned closer or recap phrase; stop after the last new fact or give the next action.

- Threshold: **standard:** listed phrase opening a final sentence or paragraph, or a Conclusion section in a short piece · **strict:** any listed closer anywhere · **relaxed:** only 'in conclusion / to sum up' recaps that repeat earlier text
- Triggers: `in conclusion`, `overall`, `ultimately`, `to wrap up`, `in summary`, `to summarize`, `to sum up`, `at the end of the day`, `a key takeaway is`, `the bottom line is`, `conclusion`
- Exceptions: 'overall' and 'ultimately' mid-text in their literal sense; a real summary section in long reports, specs or papers where the genre expects one; an executive summary at the top
- Example: ✗ In summary, caching makes the site faster. → ✓ (end after the benchmark table)

### LEX-028 · formulaic challenge / outlook closers
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Cut generic future-outlook and despite-challenges formulas unless they name the challenge, the response, or a testable prediction.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `a step in the right direction`, `as we move forward`, `awards and recognition`, `challenges and legacy`, `continues to thrive`, `despite its`, `despite ongoing challenges, x continues to thrive`, `despite these challenges`, `exciting possibilities lie ahead`, `exciting times ahead`, `faces several challenges`, `future outlook`, `future prospects`, `looking ahead, x will play an increasingly pivotal role`, `one thing is certain`, `only time will tell`, `poised to become one of the most`, `the future looks bright`
- Exceptions: specific, sourced difficulties and forecasts; a real risks section that names specific problems and their status; real plans the source states
- Example: ✗ Despite challenges, the project continues to thrive and may become one of the defining tools of the decade. → ✓ Funding ends in March; the team is applying for two grants.

### LEX-029 · chatbot residue and sycophancy
`hard · ai-tell · scope: all · voice cannot override`

Remove chatbot wrapping from deliverable text: greetings, praise of the question, agreement tics, offers of more help and sign-offs; keep the content.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `absolutely!`, `absolutely! here's what you need`, `certainly!`, `certainly! i'd be happy to`, `certainly, here are`, `changes:`, `curious to hear your thoughts`, `don't hesitate to ask if you need more information!`, `excellent point`, `feel free to reach out`, `feel free to reach out if you have questions!`, `found the smoking gun!`, `great question`, `great question!`, `here is a`, `here is a comprehensive`, `here's a comprehensive overview`, `hope this finds you well`, `hope this helps`, `i hope this helps`, `i hope this helps!`, `i'd love your perspective`, `i'd value your take on this`, `improvements:`, `in this article, we will explore`, `is there anything else`, `let me know`, `let me know if`, `let me know if you need anything else`, `let me know if you need anything else!`, `love this`, `more detailed breakdown`, `of course!`, `of course! let me`, `should i continue`, `should i continue?`, `sure! here's`, `that's a really insightful observation`, `want me to`, `what a great idea`, `would you like`, `you're absolutely right`, `you're absolutely right!`
- Exceptions: in a live chat reply to the user, one specific, concrete next-step offer is allowed (see C-A-11); quoted dialogue; a correction of the user stated plainly without flattery; genuine, specific feedback the user asked for (a review); a chat reply to the user (not deliverable text) may end with one concrete question; emails and letters where the writer's own convention includes a closing line; quoted material; a genuine reply message where a closing line is the writer's convention; letter or comment sign-offs (see PRC-018)
- Example: ✗ Great question! Here's a comprehensive overview... I hope this helps! → ✓ (the overview only)

### LEX-030 · cutoff, refusal and info-gap disclaimers
`hard · ai-tell · scope: all · voice cannot override`

Never leave knowledge-cutoff notes, as-an-AI refusals or narration of missing information in deliverable text; state what is known or leave the point out.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `as a large language model`, `as an ai language model`, `as of my last knowledge update`, `as of my last update`, `based on available information`, `based on the information provided`, `details are limited`, `i cannot offer medical advice`, `i don't have access to real-time data`, `i'm sorry`, `in the provided sources`, `in the search results`, `it is believed that`, `likely began`, `not publicly available`, `not widely available`, `not widely documented`, `up to my last training update`, `while specific details are limited`, `while specific details are limited based on available information`
- Exceptions: an explicit, user-requested statement of research limits in a report's methods section; integrity: do not replace the disclaimer with an invented fact
- Example: ✗ While specific details are limited in available sources, the town likely has a market. → ✓ The town has a Thursday market. (or omit the sentence)

### LEX-031 · reasoning leaks and meta-commentary
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Do not leak process into the deliverable: no reasoning-chain scaffolding, no narration of the text's own structure, no meta-commentary about what the piece will do.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `let me think step by step`, `breaking this down`, `to approach this systematically`, `here's my thought process`, `first, let's consider`, `working through this logically`, `you already know this, but`, `but that's another post`, `the rest of this essay explains...`, `let me walk you through...`, `in this section, we'll...`, `as we'll see...`, `i want to explore...`
- Exceptions: a document map in long docs ('Section 3 covers deployment') when navigation needs it; tutorials that legitimately walk through steps
- Example: ✗ Let me think step by step. In this section, we'll explore the parser. → ✓ The parser reads tokens left to right.

### LEX-032 · leaked tool tokens and placeholders
`hard · ai-tell · scope: all · voice cannot override`

Strip leaked chat-citation tokens, AI-referrer tracking parameters and unfilled placeholders before delivering text.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `2025-xx-xx`, `<!-- add citation if available -->`, `[attached_file:1]`, `[cite:`, `[describe the specific section]`, `[insert source url]`, `[your name]`, `attached_file`, `attributableindex`, `citeturn0search0`, `contentreference`, `contentreference[oaicite:0]`, `grok_card`, `oai_citation`, `oaicite`, `ppl-ai-file-upload`, `referrer=grok.com`, `start_span`, `turn0search`, `utm_source=chatgpt.com`, `utm_source=claude.ai`, `utm_source=copilot.com`, `utm_source=openai`, `utm_source=perplexity.ai`
- Exceptions: keep functional query parameters; template files whose purpose is to contain placeholders; a token shows tool involvement, not authorship; text that discusses these tokens as its subject
- Example: ✗ See the docs (https://x.dev/a?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [INSERT SOURCE URL] → ✓ See the docs (https://x.dev/a).

### LEX-033 · vague attribution (weasel words)
`hard · both · scope: prose · voice cannot override`

Name the source behind a claim instead of unnamed experts, studies or reports; if no source is available, flag the gap or drop the claim.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `according to sources`, `analysts agree`, `described in scholarship`, `experts agree`, `experts argue`, `experts believe`, `experts say`, `featured in`, `independent testing confirms`, `industry leaders`, `industry leaders agree`, `industry reports`, `industry reports suggest`, `multiple publications`, `observers have cited`, `observers have noted`, `over n followers`, `research suggests`, `several publications`, `several sources`, `some critics`, `some critics argue`, `studies show`, `third-party benchmarks show`, `widely regarded`
- Exceptions: the source is named nearby in the same paragraph; never invent a source to satisfy this rule; the named source is given in the same sentence or a citation; the vague phrasing is inside a quotation; a named body of consensus is given ("the WHO", "the Rust reference"); 'such as' introducing a real non-exhaustive list is fine
- Example: ✗ Studies show that monorepos speed up teams. → ✓ Google's 2016 paper reports X; we have no data for teams our size.

### LEX-034 · vague association
`default · both · scope: prose · voice cannot override`

Replace vague 'associated with / connected to' links with the actual relationship when the source gives it; if it does not, keep the vague wording rather than invent a role.

- Threshold: **standard:** any occurrence where the source states the relation; 2+ unexplained per piece · **strict:** any single occurrence · **relaxed:** 2+ per paragraph
- Triggers: `associated with`, `in association with`, `connected to`, `in connection with`, `linked to`, `tied to`, `connected with`, `became associated with`, `widely associated`
- Exceptions: statistical association (correlation) in data writing; integrity: do not upgrade an unknown relationship into a specific one
- Example: ✗ She is associated with the Halden Choir, which she founded. → ✓ She founded the Halden Choir.

### LEX-036 · aphorisms and hidden-truth framing
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Replace deep-sounding aphorisms, hidden-truth framings and quotable one-liners with the specific claim they gesture at.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `the real question is`, `at its core`, `in reality`, `what really matters`, `fundamentally`, `the deeper issue`, `the heart of the matter`, `the language of`, `the currency of`, `the architecture of`, `becomes a trap`, `not a tool but a mirror`, `make no mistake`, `the truth is`, `x is the language of y`
- Exceptions: quotations and established idioms; a single memorable line the voice profile owns, backed by the paragraph
- Example: ✗ Latency is the currency of trust. → ✓ Pages that load in under a second keep more users in our tests.

### LEX-037 · announced significance
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not announce that something is hard, significant or contrarian; show the difficulty or stakes with the specific detail.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `this is genuinely hard`, `this is what leadership actually looks like`, `this is what x actually looks like`, `actually matters`, `the reasons are structural`, `the implications are significant`, `this is the deepest problem`, `the stakes are high`, `the consequences are real`, `that last move is the contrarian one`
- Exceptions: a topic sentence immediately followed by the evidence
- Example: ✗ The implications are significant. → ✓ Every client must re-authenticate after the change.

### LEX-038 · performed insight and novelty inflation
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Cut performed-insight tics, novelty-inflation and crowd-contrast framing (what nobody tells you, while everyone else debated); name a crowd or a gap only if the source does.

- Threshold: **standard:** any novelty or crowd claim; performed-insight tics at 2+ per piece · **strict:** any single occurrence · **relaxed:** 2+ per piece
- Triggers: `sit with that for a moment`, `that's not nothing`, `you already know the answer`, `don't take my word for it`, `that's the whole point`, `is the entire business model`, `that's the part nobody mentions`, `the only metric that matters`, `that's why it mattered`, `turns out`, `he introduced a term`, `she coined the phrase`, `a concept nobody's naming`, `a failure mode nobody talks about`, `the insight everyone's missing`, `what nobody tells you about`, `most people don't realize`, `everyone's sleeping on`, `the truth nobody talks about`, `what nobody's saying`, `while everyone else was still debating`, `the call most leaders won't make`
- Exceptions: 'turns out' in casual voice once, when reporting an actual finding; a documented, cited claim that a topic is under-studied
- Example: ✗ Here's the failure mode nobody talks about. That's not nothing. → ✓ Retries can double load during an outage.

### LEX-039 · performed sincerity and reader management
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Remove narrated candor, lingering-attention claims, stock reactions and reader-management lines (I want to be upfront, I can't stop thinking about, think about it, and that's okay, I promise); keep the disclosure or fact itself.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `i would rather flag`, `i want to be upfront`, `to be fully transparent`, `rather than bury this`, `i could have left this out`, `being honest about the limitations`, `in the interest of full disclosure`, `the line i keep coming back to`, `i can't stop thinking about this`, `still thinking about this one`, `rattling around in my head`, `i've been chewing on this`, `what surprised me most`, `i was fascinated to discover`, `what struck me was`, `i was excited to learn`, `the most interesting part`, `interesting part of the project`, `hits different`, `creeps in`, `i promise`, `they exist, i promise`, `think about it:`, `and that's okay.`
- Exceptions: real conflict-of-interest disclosures; an authentic stated reaction with a reason attached; the user's own voice when the profile shows it
- Example: ✗ I want to be upfront: this is slower. Think about it. → ✓ This is 20% slower.

### LEX-040 · no mechanical synonym swaps
`hard · procedure · scope: all · voice cannot override`

When removing a flagged word, rewrite the thought rather than swapping in a synonym, and never make one replacement word your new default.

- Exceptions: do not remove a word used in its legitimate, literal or technical sense
- Example: ✗ delve into -> explore (in every paragraph) → ✓ We will delve into the logs -> The logs show two timeouts at 03:10.

### LEX-041 · phantom objections and false concessions
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not argue with objections nobody raised, stage vague concessions, or invent a phantom opposite to mirror a term; keep real objections the text attributes and answers.

- Threshold: **standard:** any phantom objection or vague-both-halves concession; several in a row is a strong tell · **strict:** any single occurrence · **relaxed:** 2+ per piece
- Triggers: `this isn't mainly about`, `i'm not saying`, `to be clear`, `don't get me wrong`, `this is not to say`, `some might say`, `a tempting approach would be`, `one might be tempted to`, `you might think`, `it would be easy to just`, `you might think... but`
- Exceptions: an objection attributed to a named party or fully answered; an alternative a reader would genuinely weigh; factual tradeoffs with concrete halves; temporal 'while'
- Example: ✗ A tempting approach would be to restart the service, but that drops sessions. Rotation happens in place. → ✓ Rotation happens in place.

### LEX-044 · formulaic headers and listicle counts
`soft · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not use hollow default headings (Overview, Key Points, Conclusion) or listicle counts (five things to know) when a specific heading would say more.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `overview`, `key points`, `summary`, `conclusion`, `introduction`, `three key takeaways`, `five things to know`, `here are the top seven`
- Exceptions: genre-required sections (Overview in a design doc template, Summary in a paper); repo or doc-site convention
- Example: ✗ ## Key Takeaways → ✓ ## Why the cache misses on deploy

### LEX-047 · technical terms: standard and defined
`default · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

Use the established technical term when it is the most precise option and define it briefly when readers may not know it; do not coin shorthand to replace a standard term.

- Exceptions: text for specialists who already know the term: no definition needed
- Example: ✗ We reconcile via the sync-flip approach. → ✓ We reconcile with a two-phase commit (the coordinator asks every node to prepare, then to commit).
